Hi Liam / Jonas — Karthik here. Below is a concise technical summary that should map to the audit boxes. I'll attach a simple SVG flow and a sanitized expunge log sample.

Scope notes (GreenBank EU tenants):
- Primary snapshots: retained in eu-west-1 block storage snapshots (encrypted at rest with customer kms alias).
- DR replicas: asynchronous cross-region copies to eu-central-1 for failover; these copies are metadata-linked snapshots, not hot mountable copies.
- Offsite archival: 30-day cold archive for automated DR runs (configurable per-customer).

Deletion propagation (typical flow):
1) Deletion request / TTL expiry: service marks object as "deleted" (tombstone) in metadata index — immediate (sub-second at write path).
2) Tombstone propagation: tombstones are batched and replicated with the next snapshot replication window (~15–90 minutes depending on active batching and current load).
3) Replica pruning: replica nodes run compaction jobs hourly; tombstone marking leads to object dereference. Physical expunge only occurs after compaction and offsite sweep.
4) Final expunge / expunge wave: background expunge runs sweep storage manifests and remove data blobs; typical time-to-final-expunge: 72–168 hours post-tombstone under normal operations.

Caveats and controls:
- Legal hold: placed at the tenant level — legal hold overrides TTL and prevents tombstone from expunge waves until cleared. We retain a per-tenant legal-hold flag propagated to replica/archival queues.
- Failover overlap: during cross-region failover, some replicas are kept read-only for a limited window (48–96 hours) — we can narrow that window with dedicated policies for Enterprise/Dedicated customers.
- KMS key rotation / deletion: destruction of customer KMS keys is irreversible and will render snapshots unreadable; key destruction is separate from expunge and has its own governance.

Audit evidence we can provide (examples):
- Expunge manifest extract (timestamped, lists object ids removed) — sample attached (sanitized).
- Snapshot replication trace (time-series showing tombstone creation and replication ack).
- Config snapshot showing legal-hold flags and retention policy applied to the tenant.
- Short attestation letter (signed by Redwood security) describing the flow and citing relevant system logs (production-grade statement).

Attachments: redwood-backup-deletion-flow.svg (diagram), expunge-log-sample.txt (sanitized manifest).

Happy to expand any specific part of the timeline if you need to show evidence to an external regulator.

— Karthik Iyer
